key_insight: LLM agents struggle to reliably assemble high-fidelity MBPT workflows on their own, but an expert-curated, deterministic framework can make GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT calculations runnable and consistent.
engineering_relevance: This work shows that reliable agentic automation in computational materials science requires encoded domain knowledge and controlled execution, not just a stronger model.
method: Benchmarked frontier and open-weight LLM agents on GW, GW-BSE, and GWPT workflow construction.
Built AI-Donkey, combining expert-curated workflow knowledge with deterministic execution.
Demonstrated autonomous calculation and post-processing on 1D, 2D, and bulk materials.
evidence_signal: Out-of-the-box agent performance averaged 54% on GW, 36% on GW-BSE, and 19% on GWPT benchmarks, with large run-to-run variation that disappeared under AI-Donkey.
watch_item: The framework likely depends on careful expert curation and may need continuous updates as software stacks, parameters, and MBPT best practices evolve.
paper_title: Enabling large language model agents for high-fidelity many-body perturbation theory calculations
